item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":0,"rationale":"This segment only recites statutory requirements and authority; it does not itself direct executive action or change any legal consequence.","evidence":"Section 502(d)(1) of the Trade Act (19 U.S.C. 2462(d)(1)) provides that the President may withdraw, suspend, or limit the application of duty-free treatment"},{"segment_id":"2","code":3,"rationale":"The President makes the statutory determination suspending Belarus's GSP benefits; the trade consequence follows from this present presidential act.","evidence":"I have determined that it is appropriate to suspend Belarus's GSP benefits"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The President states a determination that an HTS modification is appropriate but does not perform that modification in this segment.","evidence":"I have determined that it is appropriate to modify general note 4(a)"},{"segment_id":"4","code":3,"rationale":"The President presently makes the statutory high-income determination that triggers termination under the cited statute.","evidence":"I have determined that Malta, French Polynesia, New Caledonia, and Slovenia meet the definition of a \"high income\" country"},{"segment_id":"5","code":3,"rationale":"The President expressly terminates preferential tariff treatment as of a specified effective date.","evidence":"I am terminating the preferential treatment under the GSP"},{"segment_id":"6","code":3,"rationale":"The proclamation itself modifies the HTS country lists, thereby ending specified GSP treatment on the stated effective dates.","evidence":"general note 4(a) of the HTS is modified by deleting \"Belarus\" from the list of independent countries"}]}
